\chapter{Wanting, Not Asserting}
\label{ch:spanish-quiero-que}
\hlchaptermodality{78}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can tell an asserted event apart from a wanted one, and say why the verb changes.}

Hablas espanol asserts; quiero que hables asserts nothing at all.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Hablas español · Quiero que hables español]{Hablas español · Quiero que hables español — fact or wanted event?}

\label{lesson:ES-C18-quiero-que}



\begin{quote}
\textbf{Hablas español} can assert “You speak Spanish.” Now compare \textbf{Quiero que hables español} — “I want you to speak Spanish.” \textbf{Hables} does not report what is true. It presents the speaking as wanted and not yet asserted. That meaning contrast is the first small doorway into the \textbf{subjunctive}.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: count the doers}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{meaning} & \textbf{Spanish} & \textbf{doers} \\
\midrule
I want to speak Spanish. & \textbf{Quiero hablar español.} & one: I want; I speak \\
I want you to speak Spanish. & \textbf{Quiero que hables español.} & two: I want; you speak \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

With one doer, keep the known infinitive \textbf{hablar}. With a different doer for the wanted event, use \textbf{que} and the new form \textbf{hables}. This is a bounded pattern for \textbf{querer}, not a rule for every clause in Spanish.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item “Hablas español.”
  \item “Quiero hablar español.”
  \item “Quiero que hables español.”
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which form asserts the event? (\textbf{Hablas.}) Which presents it as wanted? (\textbf{Hables}, after \textbf{quiero que}.) What happens when the wanter and the speaker are the same? (Use the infinitive: \textbf{Quiero hablar}.) Next, build the three singular \textbf{-ar} forms one piece at a time.
\end{tcolorbox}
